sources.title: Personally executed frozen inline program, exercise and original Kev pure nodes on CPU
Reviewer symbolic derivation of permutation, collision and normalization properties
sources.details: Manual symbolic algebra, not a claim of executed floating-point evaluation: Let q depend only on fixed state/question and let the same candidate map produce rows K. For any permutation matrix P on a nonempty fixed real-candidate list, K_new=P K, so s_new=P K q/sqrt(d)=P s. max(P s)=max(s), hence the lesson's none=1-max(s) is unchanged. With P_ext=diag(P,1), exp(P_ext z)=P_ext exp(z) and the sum of the same exponentials is unchanged; therefore softmax(P_ext z)=P_ext softmax(z) over real candidates plus none. The maximizing ID set is unchanged, so selecting the lexicographically first unique fixed ID also commutes with reordering. Mean, max and count are mathematically symmetric summaries; this says nothing about whether none predicts the correct target. Adding/removing an item changes the collection and can change max and the sum of exponentials, so no same-probability guarantee follows. Shared maps with interactions can remain equivariant: g_i(X)=lambda*x_i+gamma*sum_j(x_j) satisfies g(PX)=P g(X), and a symmetric readout is invariant; Deep Sets §3.1 supplies the original constructive architecture. A causal prefix instead changes with order: with card=(1,0), address=(0,1), q=(2,0), card-first gives address key=(0.5,1), whereas address-first gives address key=(0,1). Their scaled scores are 1/sqrt(2) and 0; the card score is sqrt(2) in both orders. Finally if both candidate features are (0,1), the identical shared map gives identical keys and scores for any fixed q, so an ID tie rule cannot recover the lost card/address distinction. The exp/softmax decimal evaluations are separately marked executed in a_execution. Real-valued mathematical permutation identities are not promises of bit-identical arbitrary floating-point reductions.
